query: Explain why some Qatar Airways Business-Class flights receive a non-recommended (Recommended = no) result.

per_column.name: downgrade_notification_failure
per_column.rationale: A candidate cause (service failure event) whose effect on non-recommendation is being attributed; a plausible treatment surfaced from review text, not named in the query.

per_column.name: seat_hardware_quality
per_column.rationale: Physical seat condition (functional vs defective/cramped) is a candidate cause of dissatisfaction driving non-recommendation. Overlaps with existing Seat Comfort rating; acts as a driver/treatment rather than a common cause of another treatment.

per_column.name: onboard_amenity_quality
per_column.rationale: Amenity provisioning quality is another candidate driver of the outcome, not a common cause that also determines other treatments; functions as a parallel treatment/driver, not a confounder.

per_column.name: cabin_crew_service_quality
per_column.rationale: Service quality is a direct driver of recommendation; overlaps with existing Staff Service. A parallel candidate cause, not a common cause of the other treatments.

per_column.name: service_consistency_across_sectors
per_column.rationale: Sector/route composition (whether service varies by sector) plausibly drives which service failures occur AND the outcome, making it a route-level common cause that should be adjusted for. Surfaced from data, not named in query.

judge.rationale: The added columns clearly supply candidate TREATMENTS (downgrade failure, seat hardware, amenities, crew service) whose effects on non-recommendation are being attributed, and none of these were named in the query, so (a) is satisfied. However, the set is essentially a bundle of parallel DRIVERS of the outcome rather than genuine CONFOUNDERS -- variables that are common causes of BOTH a treatment and the outcome. Only 'service_consistency_across_sectors' arguably operates as a route/sector-level common cause that could bias attribution if unadjusted, and even that reads more as another outcome-adjacent quality signal. There is no adjustment variable such as route, aircraft type, traveller segment, or seat position that plausibly causes both a specific service failure and the recommendation. Thus the decisive test -- surfacing real confounders that must be adjusted to de-bias the attribution -- is only weakly met, and the causal-estimation setup is incomplete.
